# Roadmap

A family of small, native macOS apps: private, open source, free forever.

## record-0.1 — Common Record 0.1: short screen recordings, straight to the clipboard

`··········` 0% · 0 of 6 done

Press a shortcut, choose an area, a window or the screen the way Common Shot does, and stop with the same shortcut: a short MP4 lands on the clipboard and in a corner preview, small enough to attach to a pull request, an issue or a chat without a trip through an editor.

## window-0.1 — Common Window 0.1: window layouts from the keyboard

`··········` 0% · 0 of 6 done

Put the frontmost window exactly where it belongs with one shortcut: a half, a third, a quarter, the middle, or the other display. Pressing again cycles through the sizes that make sense. Arrangements you save come back when you dock to the same displays.

## sound-0.1 — Common Sound 0.1: volume and output for each app

`··········` 0% · 0 of 6 done

A menu of the apps making sound right now, each with its own volume, mute and output device: keep a call in your headphones while music plays on the speakers, or turn down one loud tab without touching everything else. Switching the Mac's own output and input is one click away.

## awake-0.1 — Common Awake 0.1: keep the Mac awake for exactly as long as something needs it

`··········` 0% · 0 of 5 done

Keep the Mac awake while a build, a download or a long agent session runs, then let it sleep on its own: for a time, until an app quits, until a command finishes, or while on power. The menu also says what else is keeping the Mac awake right now.

## color-0.1 — Common Color 0.1: pick a colour from anywhere and paste it as code

`######····` 60% · 3 of 5 done

Press a shortcut, click any pixel on any screen, and the colour is on the clipboard in the format you write: hex, CSS, SwiftUI or AppKit, converted correctly from the display's colour space. Recent picks wait in the menu, and two picks show their contrast.

## context-0.1 — Common Context 0.1: files and folders as prompt-ready text

`··········` 0% · 0 of 4 done

Select files or a folder and copy them as one block of text a model can read: a tree of what is included, then each file in a fenced block under its path, skipping what .gitignore skips and anything binary, with a token count before you paste.

## agents-0.1 — Common Agents 0.1: know when a coding agent is waiting for you

`··········` 0% · 0 of 4 done

A menu bar view of the coding-agent sessions running on this Mac, with what each is doing, and a notification the moment one needs you or finishes, so a long session never sits idle waiting for an answer nobody saw.
